keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «우리가 쓰는 언어가 생각하는 방식을 바꿀까?(질문)» 와 «언어는 마음을 가두는 감옥이 아니라 주의를 이끄는 도구다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the question (does the language you speak change the way you think?) and the conclusion (language is a tool that guides attention rather than a prison that traps the mind). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why can the five-year-old girl point to north even inside a building?
qs.qko: 다섯 살 소녀는 왜 건물 안에서도 북쪽을 가리킬 수 있나요?
opts: Her language uses compass directions for everything
She always carries a compass in her pocket
Her teacher showed her a map of the building
evs: For her, this is completely normal, because her language uses compass directions for everything.
This question has fascinated scientists for nearly a century.
People can learn new concepts, and translation between languages is possible.
why: 본문에 그 아이의 언어는 모든 것을 동서남북 방향으로 말한다고 나와요. 그래서 방향을 늘 의식하게 돼요.
The text says her language uses compass directions for everything, so she always keeps track of directions.

qs.q: In the text, what does "that strong version" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «that strong version(그 강한 형태)» 은 무엇을 뜻하나요?
opts: The idea that we cannot think about things our language has no words for
The idea that language guides what we notice
The idea that translation between languages is easy
evs: In the early twentieth century, the linguist Benjamin Lee Whorf suggested that language strongly shapes thought.
In its strongest form, this idea says we cannot think about things our language has no words for.
Language may not limit thought, but it can influence what we notice and remember.
Even so, these effects are usually small, and scientists still debate how far they go.
why: 앞에서 언어가 생각을 크게 좌우한다는 생각이 나오고, 그 가장 강한 형태는 «자기 언어에 단어가 없는 것은 생각할 수 없다» 는 주장이라고 해요. 그것이 «strong version» 이에요.
The idea that language strongly shapes thought, in its strongest form, says we cannot think about things our language has no words for. That is the strong version.

qs.q: How does the Korean language guide what speakers pay attention to?
qs.qko: 한국어는 말하는 사람이 무엇에 주의를 기울이도록 이끄나요?
opts: Honorifics make speakers notice age and relationships when they choose words
Korean has more words for colors than Russian
Korean speakers always describe places with north and south
evs: Its system of honorifics requires speakers to pay constant attention to age and social relationships.
For example, you say a polite greeting to a teacher but a short, casual one to a close friend.
Russian has separate basic words for light blue and dark blue, and studies suggest Russian speakers can tell these shades apart slightly faster.
People can learn new concepts, and translation between languages is possible.
why: 한국어의 높임법은 말하는 사람이 나이와 관계에 늘 신경 쓰게 만들고, 그래서 선생님께는 공손하게, 친한 친구에게는 짧고 편하게 인사해요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
Korean honorifics require attention to age and relationships, so you greet a teacher politely and a close friend casually. You need both sentences.

ends: How do people who use compass directions find their way?
